title: Watchfulness, again
hookLine: knowing He sees you, recalled from earlier in the path

lines: A SHEPHERD BOY IN THE HILLS.
cards: A boy is minding a flock of sheep in the hills. A traveler comes by, the companion Abdullah ibn Umar, so the story goes, and tests him. Sell me one sheep, he says.
Tell your master a wolf took it. Who would know? The boy looks at him and answers with a question: then where is Allah?
It's a story people tell, found in later collections rather than the major hadith books. But the boy's answer holds today's whole lesson.

teach.b: The word is muraqabah, watchfulness: living with the awareness that Allah sees you. We met the idea much earlier in the path, with ihsan.
In the hadith of Jibril, in Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim, the angel asks the Prophet, peace be upon him, what ihsan is.

teach.h: IHSAN: IF YOU DON'T SEE HIM, HE SEES YOU.
teach.b: The answer: to worship Allah as though you see Him, and if you don't see Him, He sees you. That second half is muraqabah. You may not feel the presence; the watching doesn't depend on your feeling it.
The Qur'an says it plainly, in Pickthall's translation: "Lo! Allah hath been a Watcher over you." And elsewhere, that He is with you wherever you are. Why come back to it after repentance?
Because the stations lean on each other.
Tawbah turns you around. Muraqabah keeps you turned; without it, a person who has just made amends can drift right back. Notice that the shepherd boy isn't afraid of being caught.
Nobody is there to catch him. What stops him is simpler: he knows he's seen. That's the difference between watchfulness and anxiety.
It isn't a security camera that makes you nervous. It's closer to how you speak differently when someone you love is in the room.

Teachers of the path describe it as a steady awareness of the heart, in prayer and outside it, showing up in small places: the receipt you could fudge, the comment you could post anonymously, the shortcut nobody would notice.

how: In the Islamic inward path, muraqabah is the cultivated awareness that Allah sees, drawn from the hadith of Jibril; some Sufi orders also use the word for a practice of quiet, attentive sitting.

o: watchfulness: living aware that Allah sees you
a night watch spent guarding a city's walls
keeping a close eye on what other people do

p: worship as though you see Him

s: muraqabah means feeling Allah's presence at every moment
the hadith says: if you don't see Him, He sees you. the seeing doesn't depend on feeling.
the shepherd boy story is in the major hadith collections
it's a story people tell, found in later collections.
the Qur'an speaks of Allah as a watcher
Pickthall's translation of 4:1: Lo! Allah hath been a Watcher over you.

games.q: you're the shepherd boy. a stranger offers to buy a sheep and says: tell your master a wolf took it. who would know?
o: ask him: then where is Allah?
games.why: in the story people tell, the boy answers with a question, and the man testing him, said to be Ibn Umar, is moved by it.

practice: Let your shoulders drop and hold one thought, without forcing it: I am seen, right now, as I am, not judged, not graded, seen. Notice what shifts in your body, and when your mind wanders, come back to the thought.
If you pray, rest in the hadith's line, if you don't see Him, He sees you; if not, simply rest in being seen.

wordCard.voice: Muraqabah. Watchfulness: living with the awareness that Allah sees you, the second half of ihsan. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: he sees. Not a camera that watches you, but a presence that stays. See you tomorrow.
